description: Ability to review, interpret, and verify the quality, completeness, and accuracy of AI/automation-generated literature reviews, summaries, and synthesized datasets; includes understanding limits of automation and recognizing potential algorithmic bias.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups, applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.'
change to work: This will shift from hands-on manual research and data synthesis to a more oversight-driven function: the officer will review and validate literature/data research carried out by automation, focus on identifying gaps/misclassifications in AI-produced outputs, and provide domain-specific interpretation for nuanced or context-sensitive cases. They will also need to understand the limitations and potential biases of automated outputs.
justification: As more literature review and data synthesis are automated, skill will be required to critically assess AI-generated content for accuracy, completeness, and bias.

description: Capacity to provide effective feedback or corrections to improve automated workflows, tune AI system outputs, and communicate contextual needs to technical teams.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups, applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.'
change to work: This will shift from hands-on manual research and data synthesis to a more oversight-driven function: the officer will review and validate literature/data research carried out by automation, focus on identifying gaps/misclassifications in AI-produced outputs, and provide domain-specific interpretation for nuanced or context-sensitive cases. They will also need to understand the limitations and potential biases of automated outputs.
justification: Officers must now provide feedback and supervisorial guidance to AI system design or configuration, suggesting how outputs can be improved for policy relevance or analytic nuance.

description: Basic understanding of how automation and AI systems aggregate, synthesize, or select information; ability to spot errors, gaps, or biases in digital outputs and explain why certain sources/outputs are or are not relevant.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Research and Analysis - 'Undertakes literature and data research in support of Statistics Canada evaluation studies, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager. The position identifies and recommends to the Evaluation Manager the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies.'
change to work: The focus will move from manual search/discovery and data mining to: (a) evaluating the relevance and accuracy of literature/data sources identified by AI systems; (b) determining the strategic value of results surfaced by automated systems; and (c) recommending fixes or further investigation when automated results are insufficient.
justification: Understanding and validating AI-driven data source selection or automated literature review requires digital and analytic literacy.

description: Awareness of the strengths, weaknesses, and suitable use cases for automated data retrieval and synthesis techniques—enabling evidence-based recommendations and risk identification.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations. Recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses.'
change to work: Interpreting findings will increasingly include scrutinizing AI-generated summaries, recommending refinements to retrieval/analysis algorithms, and deciding which insights require deeper manual follow-up or contextual adjustment.
justification: To recommend method enhancements and interpret AI-driven outputs, officers will need a working knowledge of AI/automation methods in data retrieval and synthesis.

description: Ability to explain, contextualize, and document the use and results of automated processes to both technical and general audiences, including caveats, limitations, and human intervention points.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Communication - 'The incumbent is required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process; prepare statistical and narrative summaries for review by the Evaluation Manager, provide progress reports, and brief the Evaluation Manager on the activities and processes being followed.'
change to work: There will be an increasing emphasis on communicating how AI-driven findings were reached, explaining what was automated versus what required human intervention, and discussing any limitations or interpretive nuances in machine-generated outputs.
justification: Officers will need to clearly explain the process and implications of AI/automation use to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

description: Basic knowledge of how AI/automation changes evaluation study workflows and data quality, and how to apply social science rigor to algorithmic findings.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Knowledge of Specialized Fields - 'Knowledge of theories, methods and techniques of research, including social science research and analysis in order to: undertake literature and data research in support of Statistics Canada evaluation studies; identify, synthesize and analyze qualitative and quantitative research data; conduct interviews and participate in focus groups.'
change to work: Must expand beyond traditional discipline knowledge to include how automation and AI systems operate in research contexts: their methodologies, common pitfalls, and how outputs differ from manual work.
justification: Expertise now includes knowing when and how to apply, validate, and critique digital/AI-supported research techniques.

description: Ability to assess, filter, and validate automatically identified needs and research outputs, recognizing when automation might have missed or mis-categorized an important signal.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data...'
change to work: The focus will transition from manual research and need identification to: reviewing and confirming the outputs of automated, AI-driven discovery tools; interpreting the significance of needs surfaced by automation; and making recommendations on emergent or strategic topics requiring manual follow-up.
justification: With automated tools surfacing the majority of needs, officers must develop the ability to critically appraise the completeness, relevance, and contextual fit of those identifications.

description: Familiarity with how AI/automated systems aggregate and categorize data, and an ability to recognize potential errors or omissions in AI findings.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Research and Analysis - 'Collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources, including interviews, departmental documents and those of other government departments, as well as information from provincial and territorial governments and the Internet... applies established methods and techniques used for sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data.'
change to work: Rather than personally collecting large quantities of raw data, the Officer will manage, filter, and interpret data already pre-aggregated by AI tools; their analytic and interpretive skills will be used more for nuanced, complex, or missed cases rather than foundational research.
justification: Officers will need to understand automated data pipelines and their typical weaknesses or blind spots.

description: Competence at integrating AI-identified needs/data into coherent, context-rich recommendations closely linked to organizational strategy.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations.'
change to work: Their interpretive support will be increasingly focused on contextualizing results surfaced by automation, and on synthesizing complex, multi-source validation of needs prepared by AI—providing the human dimension to what may otherwise be automated triage.
justification: Ability to connect automated outputs with organizational priorities and stakeholder nuances becomes critical.

description: Ability to recognize when automated consultation/feedback syntheses are incorrect, incomplete, or miss important context, and to intervene effectively via advanced negotiation or mediation.
historic work: Key Activities: 'participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups, applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.'
change to work: While automation tools will pre-sort and synthesize stakeholder feedback or consultation records, the officer’s focus shifts to leading or mediating in-depth stakeholder engagements where AI analysis may be inadequate. They review automated summaries, validate their accuracy, and participate in high-value discussions for requirement resolution.
justification: To oversee and validate AI-analyzed consultation output, officers must develop skills in evaluating automated syntheses as well as deeper negotiation/interpersonal skills for cases AI cannot resolve.

description: Advanced skill at resolving conflicting, unclear, or evolving requirements between stakeholders, especially as flagged by technology but not fully resolved by it.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Communication - 'Speaking skills are required to discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues... to obtain data related to Statistics Canada and external evaluation studies.'
change to work: Officers will need to focus communication less on routine information gathering and more on clarifying unresolved stakeholder requirements, and on translating/mediating between AI summary outputs and nuanced stakeholder perspectives.
justification: Officers must guide discussions around sensitive or ambiguous needs not resolved by AI summaries.

development area: Interpretive Bridge Between AI and User Requirements
description: Ability to contextualize and enhance AI-catalogued requirements with real stakeholder nuance; recognizing what automation misinterprets or omits and providing amplification or correction.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases; and participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs, under supervision.'
change to work: The officer must now assess and interpret AI-extracted data requirements, validating their relevance to real-world program needs and providing recommendations for deeper analysis where automation suggests uncertainty or highlights a change.
justification: Skill in bridging between automated/AI data signal and practical, qualitative user need.

description: Ability to review, adjust, or return automated objectives and quality measures, weighing organizational, legal, and contextual factors.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations. Recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses.'
change to work: Input and recommendations now require the ability to critically evaluate, adjust, and contextualize AI-generated objectives, and to support enhancements to automated tools where necessary. The officer’s focus is on final judgment, not on manual collation or drafting.
justification: There is a need for critical assessment of machine-generated proposals for objectives and quality—officers must understand limitations or gaps in auto-drafting and act as human-in-the-loop.

development area: Interpreting Automated Quality and Output Objective Proposals
description: Understanding how AI/automation systems generate objectives and measures, and the capacity to evaluate their appropriateness in context.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Knowledge of Specialized Fields - 'Knowledge of program evaluation and performance measurement theories, processes and practices for participating in the conduct of evaluation studies, making recommendations concerning the nature and scope of studies and study approaches...'
change to work: Officers now require, in addition to foundational theory, an understanding of how automated and AI-generated objectives are formulated, how to interpret their quality and fit, and how to resolve misalignments.
justification: Knowledge must expand to encompass how technology operationalizes program evaluation and measurement criteria.

development area: Automated Business Case Review and Enhancement
description: Skill in reviewing AI/digitally-produced business case sections, identifying gaps/strategic weaknesses, and supplementing or reworking text/data for higher-level consumption and approval.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management on elements of program evaluations of various programs.'
change to work: Rather than assembling raw data/products, the officer will review automated report/briefing drafts, annotate or expand on sections needing greater context, and deliver finished or near-finished sections for management approval.
justification: With automation providing most business case content, the officer must critically appraise such content, spot missing arguments/data, and understand what decision-makers require at this level.

development area: Critical Appraisal of Automated Analytic Outputs
description: Ability to recognize logical inconsistencies or analytic flaws in automated business case sections and propose corrective action.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Research and Analysis - 'Conducts analyses and interpretation of data collected during evaluation studies under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager, as a junior member of project teams.'
change to work: The officer’s analytical role now emphasizes the interpretive and validation dimension—checking the logic and soundness of findings presented by automated systems and recognizing when additional human intervention or supplementary analysis is warranted.
justification: Must be able to discern automation's strengths and weaknesses in collation, analysis, and recommendation for business cases.

description: Ability to interpret, critique, and prioritize digital/AI evaluation outputs, recognizing context and implications for programs or policies.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager.'
change to work: The evaluation studies in which the Officer participates are now largely pre-analyzed by automation. The Officer participates by interpreting, prioritizing, and contextualizing the implications of what the automated systems surface, rather than by undertaking much of the direct evaluation data gathering or first-order analysis.
justification: Officers need to be able to make sense of, validate, and synthesize AI-generated evaluation dashboards, metrics, and action proposals.

development area: AI/Automation Bias and Limitations in Evaluation
description: Knowledge of where automated evaluation pipelines are strongest/weakest and how they may introduce systematic or contextual errors; ability to invoke additional human intervention or supplement automation as required.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data...'
change to work: Routine research, aggregation, and synthesis will be handled by AI-powered automation; the Officer will need to focus on evaluating the quality and practicality of automated research, addressing anomalies, and synthesizing insights for further review.
justification: Officers must recognize the potential biases, strengths, and blind spots of automated evaluation tools and be prepared to supplement/overrule AI where necessary.

development area: Strategic Interpretation and Communication of Automated Findings
description: Skill at translating AI-generated evaluation conclusions into actionable, stakeholder-focused findings, and at identifying recommendations that drive process improvement.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations.'
change to work: Interpretive tasks shift to deeper, higher-order analysis—explaining and contextualizing findings surfaced by AI in ways meaningful to diverse stakeholders, and identifying actionable priorities from a technology-enabled evaluation dataset.
justification: Ability to bridge automated analytic results with strategic and organizational communication and action planning.

description: Skill at critically evaluating the completeness and appropriateness of AI/LLM-collected evaluation inputs and identifying when additional input-gathering or human review is required.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data...'
change to work: Manual data and literature research is now largely replaced by the review and quality assurance of automated aggregations. Officers monitor AI/LLM systems for coverage and integrity, and may design prompts or parameter adjustments to improve input streams.
justification: Ability to assess the sufficiency, accuracy, and context of AI-harvested datasets and input summaries.

description: Ability to anticipate and detect where AI-facilitated input gathering may be incomplete, unbalanced, or contextually misaligned.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Research and Analysis - 'Collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources... applies established methods and techniques used for sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data.'
change to work: Instead of manual collection from disparate sources, the Officer is responsible for confirming the integrity and quality of the synthesized, digitally-collated body of evaluation data.
justification: Knowledge of how digital aggregation pipelines might introduce bias, miss rare signals, or over-focus on dominant inputs.

development area: Critical Review and Interpretation of Automated Evaluation Outputs
description: Ability to assess the validity, quality, and context-sensitivity of LLM/AI-generated evaluation dashboards and recommendations, and to refine or supplement them as required.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, ... analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; ... applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.'
change to work: Routine analysis and synthesis are automated; the Officer’s role shifts to higher-value synthesis: interpreting, prioritizing, and improving on what LLM/AI systems produce, identifying any misinterpretations or missed issues, and ensuring recommendations are operationally meaningful.
justification: Skills required in making sense of, critiquing, and translating automated evaluation reports into actionable proposals.

description: Knowledge of common pitfalls, strengths, and caveats of LLM/AI-based benchmarking and recommendation tools in evaluation analysis.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations.'
change to work: Interpretation is now less about direct calculation and more about comparative analysis—judging the scope and actionable value of machine-produced findings, and tailoring refinement or recommendations for varying audiences.
justification: Understanding of the scope, limits, and intended use of automated evaluation recommendations.

development area: Action Plan Review and Enhancement in Automated Environments
description: Competence in reviewing digital/AI-proposed action plans, contextualizing priorities, and evaluating whether automated monitoring/feedback mechanisms are functionally and strategically complete.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations. Recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses.'
change to work: Input and recommendations will increasingly focus on the validation and adjustment of AI-driven action plan drafts, the fit of digital monitoring, and the identification of improvement loops and lessons learned.
justification: Officers need the skill to appraise, refine, and communicate proposed automated plans, and to evaluate the sufficiency of automated monitoring frameworks.
